title: Knowledge, the fire that burns all karma

verses.sa: अपाने जुह्वति प्राण प्राणेऽपानं तथाऽपरे । प्राणापानगती रुद्ध्वा प्राणायामपरायणाः ॥
verses.tr: Some offer the outgoing breath into the incoming breath, and the incoming breath into the outgoing breath, restraining the movement of both through breath-control as their aim. Others, with regulated food, offer the breaths into the breaths. All of them know sacrifice and are cleansed by sacrifice.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna shows that sacrifice is not only a fire ritual. Here he speaks of breath-control and disciplined eating.

body.text: Some offer the outgoing breath into the incoming breath, and the incoming breath into the outgoing breath, restraining the movement of both through breath-control as their aim. Others, with regulated food, offer the breaths into the breaths. All of them know sacrifice and are cleansed by sacrifice. Krishna names breath-control itself as a form of sacrifice. He describes practitioners restraining the movements of the incoming and outgoing breaths and offering them into each other. He then adds regulated eating, showing that every disciplined act is a form of sacrifice.

verses.sa: अपरे नियताहाराः प्राणान्प्राणेषु जुह्वति । सर्वेऽप्येते यज्ञविदो यज्ञक्षपितकल्मषाः ॥
verses.tr: Some offer the breath into the breath through regulated breathing; some, with regulated food, offer the life-forces into the life-forces. All of them know sacrifice, and sacrifice has washed away their impurities.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is explaining that sacrifice is not just fire. He points to two specific practices. Listen for how he names the people who do them.

body.text: Some offer the breath into the breath through regulated breathing; some, with regulated food, offer the life-forces into the life-forces. All of them know sacrifice, and sacrifice has washed away their impurities. Krishna names them yajnavidah, knowers of sacrifice. He does not limit the word to priests with fire; he means anyone whose breath or food is measured is already doing the rite. He then says those who eat the nectar left over from that sacrifice attain the eternal supreme reality.

verses.sa: यज्ञशिष्टामृतभुजो यान्ति ब्रह्म सनातनम् । नायं लोकोऽस्त्ययज्ञस्य कुतो़ऽन्यः कुरुसत्तम ॥
verses.tr: Those who partake of the nectar left over from sacrifice attain the eternal supreme reality. This world is not for the one who does not perform sacrifice; how then the next world?
verses.angle: Yajna-shishta-amrita-bhujah: those who eat the nectar left over from sacrifice
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has been showing Arjuna many ways to offer action into action. Now he names the one who receives the blessed remainder.

body.text: Those who partake of the nectar left over from sacrifice attain the eternal supreme reality. This world is not for the one who does not perform sacrifice; how then the next world? Krishna calls the remainder of sacrifice nectar, and says a life without sacrifice fails even in this world. Krishna says knowing these many kinds of sacrifice born of action frees you from the bondage of action.

verses.sa: एवं बहुविधा यज्ञा वितता ब्रह्मणो मुखे । कर्मजान्विद्धि तान्सर्वानेवं ज्ञात्वा विमोक्ष्यसे ॥
verses.tr: In this way, many kinds of sacrifice are described in the sacred teaching. Know them all as born of action; knowing this, you will be freed from the bondage of action.
verses.angle: All sacrifices are born of action
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna gathers all the sacrifices he has taught and points to their common source.

body.text: In this way, many kinds of sacrifice are described in the sacred teaching. Know them all as born of action; knowing this, you will be freed from the bondage of action. The key is that every sacrifice is a karma. When Arjuna sees that even sacred ritual belongs to the realm of action, he stops clinging to the results of any ritual. Krishna now turns to the sacrifice of pure knowledge, declaring it greater than any material offering.

verses.sa: श्रेयान्द्रव्यमयाद्यज्ञाज्ज्ञानयज्ञः परन्तप । सर्वं कर्माखिलं पार्थ ज्ञाने परिसमाप्यते ॥
verses.tr: O Arjuna, knowledge-sacrifice is better than sacrifice made of material things. All action and all matter end in knowledge.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna asks: if rituals with material goods are not the highest path, what is? Listen for the term that replaces them.

body.text: O Arjuna, knowledge-sacrifice is better than sacrifice made of material things. All action and all matter end in knowledge. The word is jnana yajna, knowledge-sacrifice, and it is declared better than any sacrifice made of material things. Every action and every object ends in that knowledge. Krishna explains exactly how a seeker approaches this knowledge, through prostration, questioning, and service.

verses.sa: तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया । उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥
verses.tr: Know that by prostration, by sincere questioning, and by service. The wise who see reality will teach you that knowledge.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna shifts from giving knowledge to showing how it is received. Listen for the three steps that open the door to wisdom.

body.text: Know that by prostration, by sincere questioning, and by service. The wise who see reality will teach you that knowledge. Krishna lists three ways to receive knowledge. He calls them prostration, sincere questioning, and service. This is how one approaches those who see reality. Krishna says that with this knowledge, you will see all beings first in yourself, and then in me.

verses.sa: यज्ज्ञात्वा न पुनर्मोहमेवं यास्यसि पाण्डव । येन भूतान्यशेषेण द्रक्ष्यस्यात्मन्यथो मयि ॥
verses.tr: Knowing which, you will not fall into confusion again. Through which, you will see all beings without remainder first in yourself, and then in me.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Listen for a single word that marks a complete shift in how you see everything.

body.text: Knowing which, you will not fall into confusion again. Through which, you will see all beings without remainder first in yourself, and then in me. Once this knowledge is gained, Arjuna will see all beings in himself and then in Krishna, without confusion. Krishna says that with the raft of knowledge you will cross all wrongdoing.

verses.sa: अपि चेदसि पापेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः पापकृत्तमः । सर्वं ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं सन्तरिष्यसि ॥
verses.tr: Even if you are the worst of wrongdoers, you will cross all wrongdoing by the raft of knowledge alone.
verses.angle: Vrjinam: a weight to cross over
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just told Arjuna that seeing the self in all beings removes all confusion. Now he goes further. Listen for the one thing that can save even the worst wrongdoer.

body.text: Even if you are the worst of wrongdoers, you will cross all wrongdoing by the raft of knowledge alone. Krishna does not say the raft of knowledge washes away your wrongdoing. He says you cross over all wrongdoing by using that raft. The next verse shows that this fire of knowledge burns even action itself to ashes.

verses.sa: यथैधांसि समिद्धोऽग्निर्भस्मसात्कुरुतेऽर्जुन । ज्ञानाग्निः सर्वकर्माणि भस्मसात्कुरुते तथा ॥
verses.tr: As a blazing fire reduces fuel to ashes, so the fire of knowledge reduces all actions to ashes, Arjuna.
verses.angle: The parallel between fire and knowledge
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna carries on from his promise to Arjuna, offering one clear image of how knowledge works. Listen for the parallel.

body.text: As a blazing fire reduces fuel to ashes, so the fire of knowledge reduces all actions to ashes, Arjuna. The verse sets up one exact parallel, the blazing fire of knowledge and the blazing fire of the body. The first makes firewood into ash, and the second makes all actions into ash. Krishna declares that no other purifier in this world compares to this knowledge.

verses.sa: न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते । तत्स्वयं योगसंसिद्धः कालेनात्मनि विन्दति ॥
verses.tr: No purifier compares to knowledge in this world. The one perfected in yoga finds that knowledge within the self in time.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Arjuna has been told that knowledge burns action to ashes. Now listen to how Krishna says nothing else can wash a person clean like that knowledge.

body.text: No purifier compares to knowledge in this world. The one perfected in yoga finds that knowledge within the self in time. The word pavitram, purifying, is used here, and Krishna says no purifier equals knowledge. The yogi finds this truth inside the self, by oneself, in time. Krishna then names the exact qualities that let a person gain this knowledge and reach supreme peace.

verses.sa: श्रद्धावाँल्लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः । ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥
verses.tr: The person with trust, discipline, and controlled senses gains knowledge. Having gained knowledge, that person quickly reaches supreme peace.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna speaks from the battlefield about the one who receives knowledge. Listen to the three qualities that open the door.

body.text: The person with trust, discipline, and controlled senses gains knowledge. Having gained knowledge, that person quickly reaches supreme peace. The word shraddhavan, full of trust, names the person who receives knowledge. This inner trust opens the door to knowledge, while lack of it closes it. Krishna now names the opposite type, the doubter who has no faith and is already lost.

verses.sa: अज्ञश्चाश्रद्दधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति । नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः ॥
verses.tr: The ignorant and faithless person who doubts is ruined. For the doubter, there is neither this world, nor the next, nor happiness.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna points to a single inner state that destroys a person, a state you can hear named twice in this verse. Listen for it.

body.text: The ignorant and faithless person who doubts is ruined. For the doubter, there is neither this world, nor the next, nor happiness. The word sankhyatma means a doubting inner being. Krishna says such a person is ruined. Then he repeats that this same person finds no world, no next world, and no happiness, showing that doubt empties a person from the inside out. Krishna then says that a person whose doubts are cut away by knowledge is not bound by action, and he names Arjuna once more.

verses.sa: योगसंन्यस्तकर्माणं ज्ञानसंछिन्नसंशयम् । आत्मवन्तं न कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय ॥
verses.tr: O Dhananjaya, actions do not bind the one who has renounced action through yoga, whose doubts have been cut away by knowledge, and who abides in the true self.
verses.angle: Dhananjaya: the one who wins wealth, is freed by knowledge
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has spent the last few verses dismantling Arjuna's confusion. Now he gives the turning point: action still happens, but it no longer leaves a binding mark.

body.text: O Dhananjaya, actions do not bind the one who has renounced action through yoga, whose doubts have been cut away by knowledge, and who abides in the true self. Notice how Krishna names Arjuna, Dhananjaya, the one who won wealth. He reminds him that he is the warrior who can stand free, because yoga has loosened his hold and knowledge has cut his doubt. Krishna now commands him to cut away the final doubt with the sword of knowledge and rise to fight.

verses.sa: तस्मादज्ञानसंभूतं हृत्स्थं ज्ञानासिनाऽऽत्मनः । छित्त्वैनं संशयं योगमातिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भारत ॥
verses.tr: Therefore, O Bharata, cut away this doubt in your heart, born of ignorance, with the sword of knowledge. Stand in yoga and rise up for battle.
verses.angle: The sword of knowledge cuts the doubt in the heart
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna closes this teaching by naming the exact tool Arjuna must use to break free. Listen for it.

body.text: Therefore, O Bharata, cut away this doubt in your heart, born of ignorance, with the sword of knowledge. Stand in yoga and rise up for battle. Sanjaya, the sword of knowledge, jnanasinA (with the sword of knowledge), is not a weapon for the body but a blade of clear understanding used to cut away the doubt, samshayam (doubt), that sits in the heart, hRtstham (situated in the heart). Arjuna still cannot choose, so he asks which path is truly better for him.
